01 — Research

What I'm Building

Every project connects to the same root: making technology reach the people it hasn't reached yet — not as a statement, but as an engineering constraint.

Published · Peer-Reviewed 2025 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference on Wireless & Mobile (APWiMob) · Bali, Indonesia · Nov 2025

Adaptive Attention-Infused Predictive Learning for Scalable Genomic Sequence Compression and Fragment Reconstruction across Noisy Biomedical Repositories

Genomic archives keep growing, and they degrade: compression artifacts, storage corruption, and transmission failures fragment the very sequences that alignment, assembly, and variant calling depend on. Most work treats compression and reconstruction as two separate problems.

This paper builds one predictive framework for both — token-level predictive coding for compression, masked modelling for recovery — and benchmarks DNABERT-inspired Transformers against BiLSTM, GRU, and hybrid CNN–RNN baselines on GIAB HG002, the 1000 Genomes Project, and microbial references. Pretrained Transformers beat the recurrent and hybrid models across datasets and fragment lengths and held up better under corruption; RNNs stayed efficient on short fragments. In clinical genomics, a corrupted variant call isn't a data error — it's a missed diagnosis.

My part: model training in PyTorch and TensorFlow, and managing the preprocessing pipeline — as sixth of six authors, on a team spread across Bangladesh and the US, working under a senior researcher.

01

Reimagining NYC — Congestion Pricing & Environmental Justice

Congestion pricing was reported as an air-quality win, and inside Manhattan the numbers support that. We wanted to know where the traffic went. For the Macaulay Honors College Datathon, our team of three followed traffic and PM2.5 outward from the toll zone using MTA, Port Authority, NYC DOT, EPA and NYC Health data. Traffic rose at all three Bronx-connecting crossings the year the toll began, and PM2.5 rose beside one of them, at Throgs Neck — in a borough that holds seven of the ten districts with the highest asthma ED rates. My role: verifying the datasets and building the geospatial maps.

What the Data Showed

Inside the zone the toll appears to work: Lincoln Tunnel fell in every one of 18 monthly comparisons, and Manhattan's districts improved in NYC Health's PM2.5 data. Outside it the picture splits. RFK, Bronx-Whitestone and Throgs Neck all rose from 2024 to 2025 in both weeks tested. At Throgs Neck, bridge traffic rose 4–7% and PM2.5 in the surrounding district rose 5.0%, from 6.04 to 6.34 µg/m³. Across three EPA monitors in the Bronx, average PM2.5 climbed 28% from 2024 to 2026 (January–July), led by IS 74 at +49%; one monitor fell 9%.

How the Data Was Kept Honest

Most of the work was deciding what not to trust: 15+ government sources, pulled live through public APIs, each cross-checked against a second source where one existed. NYC DOT's traffic counters rotate locations, so year-over-year totals compared different streets until segment, date, hour and direction were matched. Two traffic feeds weren't measuring the same thing — a unit mismatch inflated one by roughly double, and 2026 looked like a collapse until they were aligned. A chart showing Throgs Neck moving the wrong way was traced to NYC Health's source data and checked against a second file. Two air-quality sources disagree about Manhattan after 2025, so both are reported. What the project can't claim stays on the page: it shows timing and pattern, not proof of cause; 2026 is a partial year; the asthma data is a 2023 baseline.

02

NeuroRoute — Hazard-Aware Emergency Routing

Standard routing treats every emergency the same. NeuroRoute doesn't. It ranks 340 NYC destinations — 145 hospitals and 195 police stations — around 44 hazard zones, weighting a cardiac case differently from a stroke, trauma, child, or general emergency, because they shouldn't be routed the same way. Deployed live.

FlaskPythonReact.jsLeaflet.jsOpenStreetMapPythonAnywhere
Child Emergency → Specialist Hospital Routing
Emergency → Nearest Police Station
Engineering Approach

Each destination is scored per query on five factors — distance, ETA, service-type match, location risk, and hazard exposure — normalised to a common scale and combined in a weighted linear combination, with separate weights per emergency category (cardiac cases weight travel time heaviest). Scores are recomputed against live inputs on every request instead of from a precomputed graph.

Tradeoffs

The weights are set heuristically from clinical triage priorities: with no labeled outcome data, a learned model would have been false precision. The natural next step is validating them against real dispatch outcomes. Per-query recomputation is cheap at 340 destinations; past a few thousand I'd move to precomputed distance matrices or a spatial index.

03

SpotB&B — A Marketplace for Private Parking

Garages in a dense city are expensive, full, or far from where you're going, while residents sit on driveways nobody knows are free. SpotB&B closes that gap: hosts list a space with the largest vehicle it fits and when it's open, and drivers search by destination, time and vehicle size and book it. The address stays hidden until a reservation is confirmed. Built with a team of five for Tech Talent Pipeline Capstone III.

How It Works

One account, two roles: anyone can drive and host. Hosts publish a listing (verified address, hourly price, availability window, the largest vehicle that fits, private arrival instructions, a photo) and manage it from a dashboard that also shows incoming bookings. Drivers choose a destination, times and vehicle size and get matching spots as cards and map markers that refresh as they pan and zoom, sorted by distance or price. Seed data covers all five boroughs, so the demo never opens on an empty screen.

Decisions the Team Made

Privacy is enforced on the server, not in the interface: exact coordinates are stored apart from rounded public ones, and the street address and arrival instructions reach only the owner and drivers with a confirmed reservation. Prices are calculated in 30-minute blocks on the server and recomputed at booking, so the browser's number is never trusted. The listing row is locked inside a database transaction while overlaps are checked, which is what prevents double-booking. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and the session lives in an HTTP-only cookie.

05 — About

How I Think

I am drawn to questions that make people uncomfortable — about power, belief, consciousness, and human behaviour. Not to provoke, but because discomfort around a question is usually a signal that the question matters. That instinct shapes everything: how I read a research paper, how I listen to a conflict between two people, how I decide what to build.

When people disagree, I don't pick a side. I look for the missing piece of information — the moment where understanding broke down before anyone raised their voice. Find that moment, and the disagreement usually resolves itself. I've applied the same method to family conflicts, to geopolitical questions, and to datasets that contradict their own authors' conclusions. Same instinct. Different scale.

"I need to understand how the whole system works before I touch any single part of it."

I study computer science and cognitive science together because the most consequential AI understands humans — it doesn't just optimise for them. For years my brain wouldn't rest, wouldn't focus, wouldn't let me work the way I needed to. Then I found jazz. Then binaural beats. Then I ended up in a neuroscience lab watching EEG readings of brains responding to sound in real time — and I realised the technology that quietly reorganised my thinking doesn't reach most people. That is not an accident. That is a design failure. And design failures, unlike accidents, can be fixed.

I was the first from my graduating class to study abroad for an undergraduate degree. My oldest brother left school when our family needed him to — so that the rest of us could continue. Several of my closest friends from childhood never made it past middle school. One of them, a brilliant dancer, was hired to perform at celebrations — a talent that had nowhere to grow. That fact sits behind every decision I make about what to research, what to build, and who to build it for.

06 — Research Vision

Questions I Keep Returning To

Not research topics. The questions that won't leave me alone.

Can AI systems understand human emotional states without reducing them to data points?

The bridge between affective neuroscience and machine learning — where BCI meets clinical psychology. How you frame the measurement changes what can be measured.

How do we build healthcare AI that stays interpretable when a life depends on the explanation?

For clinical deployment, explainability isn't a feature — it is the precondition for trust. SHAP-based XAI as architecture, not an afterthought.

How do systems fail underserved populations — and how do we engineer that failure out?

Absent technology is not neutral. It is a choice embedded in every dataset, benchmark, and deployment decision. I understand what that choice costs.

What does computational biology lose when it optimises for storage efficiency over clinical fidelity?

Genomic compression that destroys variant information isn't compression — it is loss with institutional approval. The rate–distortion tradeoff has human consequences.

07 — Inner World

The Person Behind the Work

Research tells you what someone can do. This tells you how they see.

Songs that found me

Numb — Linkin Park   ·   ای ساربان — Ey Sareban (Persian)

"All I want to do / Is be more like me / And be less like you"

That line is not rebellion. It is the exhaustion of performing a version of yourself that others are comfortable with — day after day, without rest. The Persian song comes from somewhere older: a traveller asking the caravan to slow down because he is leaving behind everyone he has ever loved. Two songs from different centuries. One feeling. The cost of becoming yourself.

Artist

Michael Jackson

The biggest star in the world — and genuinely one of the loneliest people in it. What moved me was never the spectacle. It was the vulnerability underneath. He wrote about pain, belonging, and the need to be seen across every culture. Heal the World, Man in the Mirror, They Don't Care About Us. Empathy for the voiceless at a scale most people never attempt.

Idol

Bob Marley

He turned suffering into Redemption Song — not by erasing the pain, but by insisting that the people carrying it were worth singing about. One Love is not naive optimism. It is a radical refusal to accept that some people matter less. That refusal is something I recognise.

Book

The Brothers Karamazov — Dostoevsky

Three brothers who are each certain they're right about God, love, and morality — and all of them are, partially. Dostoevsky understood that the most honest questions have no clean resolution. Faith and doubt live in the same chest. I return to it when I need to remember that carrying a contradiction isn't confusion. Sometimes it's the most honest position available.

Film

Forrest Gump

Not the running. The whole arc. A man who never tried to be extraordinary just kept showing up — through grief, war, history, and loss — without pretending to understand the systems around him. He understood people instead. Quietly, that turned out to be enough. Presence over performance.

TV · Music · Sport

Dark (German) · Jazz · Soccer

Dark: every answer opens three more questions — I watch it the way I do research, holding contradictions open until a pattern appears. Jazz while working: structured improvisation, rules that exist so you know exactly when to break them. I discovered jazz helped my brain focus in a way nothing else did — now I understand why, and it became a research direction. Soccer every week. Played for USD. Pedri is my player.

The person who sharpened me

A tech co-founder I tutor for

I tutor her younger sister in mathematics. But watching her build something from nothing — holding a vision steady while solving a hundred small problems every day — changed what I think is possible. Some people mentor through instruction. She did it through proximity.

On sound and cognition

Why jazz became a research interest

I noticed early on that certain kinds of music — jazz, binaural frequencies — organised my thinking in ways that silence didn't. I became curious about why. That curiosity led me to neuroscience, to EEG readings in a lab, to watching brains respond to sound in real time. What I found there connected directly to the work I was already building toward.
